headline_drivers: WhiteFiber Q1 2026 results: revenue $21.9M (+31% Y/Y) with $16.8M cloud and $4.8M colocation, 60.2% gross margin ex‑D&A, adjusted EBITDA $3.0M, net loss $12.0M or -$0.31 per share (company release / earnings call, 2026-05-14)
Disclosure of $921M colocation remaining performance obligations (RPO) and progress on NC‑1 data center ahead of Nscale-related revenue in Q2 2026 (company release, 2026-05-14)
Two‑year $17M cloud services contract with Hyperbolic, supporting AI / high‑performance workloads (company commentary referenced in Q1 coverage, mid‑May 2026)
Completion of MTL‑3 data center acquisition and advancement of the NC‑1 facility aimed at AI / GPU colocation workloads (company release / call, 2026-05-14)
$230M convertible notes issuance and new credit facilities, materially increasing liquidity and perceived capacity to fund AI data center build‑out (company release, 2026-05-14)

Post‑earnings bullish framing of WhiteFiber as an AI infrastructure / GPU colocation beneficiary, with multiple analysts reiterating Buy / Outperform ratings and a 6‑month median price target near $32 (QuiverQuant, TradingView, and other summaries through mid‑May 2026)

Announcement of a 10‑year, 40MW colocation agreement between subsidiary Enovum Data Centers Corp. and Nscale Global Holdings, representing roughly $865M in contracted revenue (covered in financial media / Stock Movers segment, mid‑May 2026)

Subsequent analyst bullishness and target hikes, including B. Riley lifting its target to $38 and reiterating a Buy rating after the contract news, reinforcing the AI/HPC data‑center growth narrative (reported in Perplexity-finance aggregation, mid‑May 2026)
summary:
A second, more targeted search did not uncover any hidden, marquee-customer catalyst (Apple, NVIDIA, Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Meta, Tesla, OpenAI, Anthropic, major auto OEMs, or defense primes) for WhiteFiber (WYFI) in the last 60–90 days. The available information instead points to a conventional, but still material, AI-infrastructure / balance-sheet catalyst package centered on its Q1 2026 report and capital raise.

Across the Q1 2026 press release, Gurufocus / StockTitan / TradingView recaps, QuiverQuant, and the SEC filing set, the key fundamentals are:
- Q1 2026 revenue of $21.9M, +31% Y/Y, with $16.8M from cloud services and $4.8M from colocation, 60.2% gross margin ex‑D&A, adjusted EBITDA about $3.0M, and a net loss of $12.0M (-$0.31 per share).
- Disclosure of $921M in colocation remaining performance obligations, which materially improves multi‑year revenue visibility for its data center business.
- Commentary that the NC‑1 data center is approaching initial Nscale-related revenue in Q2 2026 and that the MTL‑3 acquisition has closed, both supporting an AI / GPU-focused expansion narrative.
- A two‑year, $17M contract with Hyperbolic (an AI / cloud customer, not a mega‑cap marquee platform company), plus a $230M convertible notes issuance and new credit facilities, which ease funding constraints for build‑outs.

On the specific items requested:
- Marquee buyer: No credible report, rumor, supply‑chain note, patent analysis, or conference disclosure links WhiteFiber to Apple, NVIDIA, TSMC, Google, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta, Tesla, OpenAI, Anthropic, a major auto OEM, or a defense prime within the last 60 days. The named contract counterparty in recent coverage is Hyperbolic, which is not a household‑name Big Tech platform.
- Supply-chain research notes (Ming‑Chi Kuo, DigiTimes, Wedbush, Loop Capital, Needham, Morgan Stanley): No such research items specifically flagging WhiteFiber were found in the last 90 days in public summaries or secondary writeups.
- Design wins / qualifications / mass‑production milestones: Outside of the Hyperbolic contract and the ramp / qualification narrative for NC‑1 and MTL‑3 as AI colocation sites, there is no evidence of a specific design win like an in‑vehicle design at an auto OEM or a hardware slot in a flagship device.
- Product / platform tied to a major customer roadmap: None identified. The story is framed generically around AI / GPU colocation capacity and cloud services, not around a discrete SKU or IP block being locked into a big‑tech roadmap.
- Patents / conferences implying a marquee relationship: No publicly discussed patent filings or technical conference talks in the last ~60–90 days point to a hidden tie‑up with a marquee buyer.

In effect, the stock’s recent strength appears to be driven by: (1) the large disclosed RPO and AI‑colocation positioning of NC‑1/MTL‑3, (2) balance‑sheet strengthening via the $230M convert, and (3) follow‑on analyst and retail interest re‑rating the name as an AI infrastructure play. There is no discoverable, single marquee-customer or secret design‑win catalyst underpinning the move beyond this AI‑infra plus funding narrative.
